newsitem.title: USA: ENSR to acquire Fugro's environmental unit.
newsitem.headline: ENSR to acquire Fugro's environmental unit.

text.p: ENSR, an international environmental services firm in Acton, Massachusetts, said it signed a letter of intent to acquire Fugro N.V.'s environmental services business lines.
They include more than $50 million in revenue, 500 employees, and offices across the U.S., South America, Europe, and Africa.

The acquisition, which should be completed by the end of 1996, is subject to normal due diligence and final approval of the boards of ENSR's parent company, RWE AG. RWE is one of the largest environmental consulting, process engineering, and waste management companies in the world, the company said.

With the acquisition, ENSR will grow to a $200 million environmental services firm consisting of nearly 2,000 employees and over 50 offices around the world. The acquisition of Fugro is part of ENSR's strategic growth plans to become one of the top five environmental consulting and engineering firms in the world.
ENSR is currently the 16th largest hazardous waste firm in the country and is among the top 60 environmental service firms nationally.

Fugro has a strong international presence, especially in the U.K., the Netherlands, and South America, which will support ENSR's growing emphasis on international markets. The international market -- particularly emerging countries in Latin America, Asia, and Eastern Europe -- is the fastest growing segment of the environmental services field. ENSR is already considered a leading provider of environmental services internationally and recently announced plans to open an office in Asia.

"This acquisition creates enormous opportunity for our new organization. Fugro brings many synergistic clients, target markets, and technical services to ENSR. Coupled with their strong geographic presence and delivery systems, we will be able to expand the breadth of services our clients need to be successful," said Robert C. Petersen, President of ENSR.
A team of senior managers from ENSR and Fugro will meet after January 1 to begin evaluating the best integration of the firm's combined resources.
